reference_traces.rationale: The reviewer identified the Drosophila descending GABAergic neurons and the feeding-linked circuit as the distinctive contribution; the final paper identifies SDGs and their projection to C4da terminals.
The reviewer explicitly located the advance against prior mammalian work; the final paper likewise frames the gap as the lack of an identified descending input in larval Drosophila.
The reviewer highlighted the use of multiple nociceptor-stimulation approaches; the final paper reports convergent optogenetic, thermal, mechanical, and acute-silencing experiments.
The reviewer described an anatomical, behavioral, and calcium-imaging case for the pathway; the final paper supplies the corresponding CN-activation and C4da-response evidence.

The reviewer identified rolling as the sole nociception readout. The final paper retains rolling latency, probability, and duration as its behavioral endpoints; the author response records that the place-aversion effort did not establish an additional readout.

The reviewer asked what activates SDGs outside refeeding. The final paper supports a C4da-to-SDG activity relationship but does not identify the intervening input component, which the author response also leaves open.

The reviewer questioned whether a broader post-refeeding state could explain the behavioral effect. The final paper rules out a crawling-speed difference but does not resolve the broader-state alternative.
The reviewer asked whether suppression generalizes beyond nutritive sugars. The final paper distinguishes nutritive from nonnutritive monosaccharides but does not test proteins or fats.
Acute silencing and added genotype controls address the developmental-confound and control concerns.
The response adds GABA-based knockdown validation, independent RNAi reagents, and staining controls; the final paper incorporates independent RNAi evidence.
CN activity, direct activation, and temporally controlled InR experiments address the requested support for the refeeding pathway.
The response reports expanded behavioral samples and specifies ROI, motion-correction, and sample-unit procedures, which are reflected in the final paper.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Frame the advance as a Drosophila circuit-level implementation and distinguish it from the established mammalian literature.
limiting_points.text: Prior mammalian work had already linked feeding with nociceptive suppression and descending control, so the novelty is strongest in identifying and functionally defining this pathway in Drosophila larvae.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Maintain the explicit comparison with the previously unidentified larval descending input.
supporting_points.text: The work identifies a descending GABAergic population that gates C4da nociceptive terminals and connects sugar sensing to that control in Drosophila larvae.

questions.suggested_action: Identify the neuronal component(s) that convey activity from C4da or other inputs to SDGs in normally fed larvae.
questions.text: What circuit element activates SDGs under regular feeding conditions and closes the proposed C4da-to-SDG negative-feedback loop?

questions.suggested_action: Test state-sensitive behavioral measures that can distinguish feeding prioritization from other post-refeeding state changes.
questions.text: Does the refed phenotype reflect behavioral prioritization specifically, rather than another post-refeeding state? Unchanged crawling speed narrows, but does not resolve, that alternative.

questions.suggested_action: Compare refeeding with proteins and fats and determine whether any effect uses the same CN–insulin–SDG pathway.
questions.text: Is nociceptive suppression specific to nutritive sugars, or can other nutrient classes produce a similar response through the same pathway?

strengths.suggested_action: Preserve the cross-modality organization of the behavioral evidence.
strengths.text: Convergent thermal, mechanical, optogenetic, and chemical-stimulation experiments support SDG-dependent regulation across nociceptive modalities.

strengths.suggested_action: Retain the anatomical, physiological, and behavioral links when presenting the pathway model.
strengths.text: The study integrates anatomy, behavior, calcium imaging, and targeted neural manipulations to connect CN activity with presynaptic C4da suppression.

summary.text: The paper identifies SEZ-localized descending GABAergic neurons that suppress C4da nociceptive-terminal activity through GABAB receptors and presents a glucose-sensing CN to insulin/InR to SDG pathway associated with reduced escape rolling after refeeding.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Establish an independent nociceptive or avoidance readout with sufficient sensitivity to detect SDG modulation.
weaknesses.text: The behavioral evidence remains centered on rolling latency, probability, and duration; an independent nociception readout would test the breadth of the proposed behavioral effect.
